needs_result.text: In a five person team, coordinated per member Git branches merged through pull requests and ran the team Trello board.

Needed a voice assistant that answers in real time and can be interrupted: built it end to end as a full-stack application (React front end, FastAPI and Google ADK back end, full-duplex WebSocket) with ReAct-based agent orchestration, barge-in handling and self-hosted speech models on Docker/CUDA (float16 inference, model warm-up) to cut latency.

bullets.text: Needed an agent that researchers could trust on a cancer research platform, including when its tools fail: built a tool-calling agent (LangChain, Claude Haiku 4.5 on AWS Bedrock) for three use cases (gene alias resolution, prompt-engineered explanations of a fixed scoring pipeline, validated dataset descriptions), with deterministic Ensembl and HGNC calls, deterministic hallucination guards, and circuit breakers with a 19,213-gene parquet fallback for when the external APIs are unavailable.

Built a tool-calling LLM agent (LangChain, AWS Bedrock, Claude Haiku 4.5) for a multi-omics cancer research platform, with three tools for gene alias resolution, scoring-methodology explanation and dataset provenance.
Wrote the dissertation's AI-agent sections covering architecture, implementation and evaluation, including a documented hallucination-rate analysis and test-case outcomes.
Reviewed pull requests in the client's production repository alongside the client's CTO, the engagement's point of contact.

A product-startup client needed an agentic AI prototype turned into software their team could use: led the architecture for a five-person cross-functional team, designed hierarchical agent workflows (MCP, Exograph GraphQL, PostgreSQL for persistent storage and retrieval across agent sessions) and built the Python prototype (FastMCP, Ollama, GitHub Actions CI), then ran a live demo with client stakeholders (5-star rating from senior leadership) within the three-month engagement.

bullets.entry: Mining Insights from Customer Feedback — NLP & unsupervised analytics (MSc team project)
bullets.text: Designed the preprocessing pipeline and the clustering pipeline (K-Means, HAC, DBSCAN) across BoW, TF-IDF, Skip-gram and SBERT representations, and traced silhouette scores below 0.30 to repeated template vocabulary in the tickets.
Predicted bank-customer churn with a supervised XGBoost propensity classifier in R (tidymodels): two-stage Bayesian hyperparameter tuning, SMOTE inside the preprocessing recipe and MCC evaluation.
Deployed the agent as a Docker container on AWS Lambda (Lambda Web Adapter) with ECR image pipelines, IAM execution roles and least-privilege policies.

Wrote a three-tier test framework (tool-level, API/integration, live agent) of ~65 tests across 8 files, validated across the LLM provider migration from Groq to AWS Bedrock after a rate-limit evaluation.

Diagnosed where it struggled with a three-tier, ~65-test evaluation harness (tool-level → API → live) and hallucination-rate analysis, debugging failures layer by layer, and used the same harness to validate the Groq to Bedrock migration after a rate-limit evaluation.
